She cites HM 64 at ff. 113, 144, 145, 170, 173 too, with no other cipher word.

835.key_held: The substitution is in print by implication (Bower 2022 p. 168: C3R6SE = ceruse, M3SELLE = mesel). Not tested on the other words.

835.closed: The f. 102v cipher words are read in print: Bower 2022, p. 168 (C3R6SE = ceruse; M3SELLE / m3sel = mesel, leper), seen in the open-access PDF. That is three of the handful of cipher words in the volume and it gives the system (vowels replaced by figures). No printed reading was found for the words on ff. 111r, 163r, or whatever is on ff. 50 and 143. What is left is a few single words in a known vowel substitution, not an open cipher.

843.unvetted: Checked 9 Nov 2026 (legacy vetting batch 09). A cluster, not one cipher document, and it carries contemporary decipherments. PARES 3964726 (AHNOB FRIAS,C.28,D.1): bound register, 408 images, of letters of Oct-Dec 1645 from the Almirante de Castilla, the marqueses de los Vélez and Velada and other viceroys and ambassadors in Italy and England to the conde de Peñaranda at Münster (not to the duque de Frías, as the entry says); scope note 'Encuadernado en pergamino. Original y cifrada'. Sampled 19 openings (images 2-395, about every 25th): about a third show signed originals with passages or whole pages of numeric cipher (e.g. image 20, Palermo 24 Dec 1645, to the 'Conde de Peñaranda'; images 245, 270, 345), and beside at least two of them (images 20 and 245) a sheet in clear in a different, secretary's hand that looks like the decipherment bound in next to the letter. Which letters have a decipherment and which do not was not established: that needs all 408 images paged and each cipher letter paired with its neighbour. known.py (FRIAS,C.28,D.1; C.28,D.1; Velada): own rows only. Web search (Peñaranda Münster 1645 cartas Almirante Vélez Velada cifra Frías C.28) found nothing on the register; CODOIN 82-84 (Peñaranda's Münster correspondence) not opened. Missing: an item list of the cipher letters and whether each has its decipherment in the volume; split per key once known.

844.unvetted: Checked 9 Nov 2026 (legacy vetting batch 09). Not digitised; title only. PARES 3948678 (AHNOB FRIAS,C.1442,D.2): 'Real cédula cifrada de Felipe IV a Iñigo Melchor Fernández de Velasco, VII Duque de Frias', Madrid 29 Apr 1664, scope note 'Firma de Felipe IV. Sello de placa.', index term 'Cifra'; no extent, no images. The title shows a ciphered original, but not whether the recipient's decipherment is written on it or filed with it, which is usual for a ciphered royal order kept in the addressee's archive; and the chancery draft in clear would be in a parallel series (AGS Estado or Guerra, AHN Estado) that could not be searched by date. Neighbours checked: C.1442,D.1 is a clear real cédula to the same duke of 30 Mar 1664 (levy of 2,000 soldiers for Flanders); D.3 and D.4 are unrelated 18th-century items. known.py (FRIAS,C.1442,D.2; C.1442,D.2; Melchor Fernández de Velasco): own rows only. Web search (real cédula cifrada Felipe IV 1664 Íñigo Melchor Fernández de Velasco) and a PARES text search for the duke in 1664 found nothing more. Missing: a scan from AHNOB (Toledo) to see the cipher, its length and any decipherment on the sheet.

851.unvetted: Checked 9 Nov 2026 (legacy vetting batch 09). Not seen; box titles only, and no identifiable cipher document. NYPL MssCol 176 (Bacon cipher collection), box 15 'Riverbank Labs -- student exercises and lessons, Mexican codes' and box 16 'Riverbank Labs -- unsorted material concerning cryptography' (1982 accession sheet as quoted in the entry); not digitised. The titles do not show that any intercepted ciphertext survives, and the one account of the Riverbank boxes on record in the entry (NSA 'A great TDY') describes page proofs, student folders and exercises, with no intercepts. Riverbank and MI-8 solved the Mexican systems they worked on, so any message there would normally sit with its solution. known.py (MssCol 176; Riverbank; Mexican codes): own rows, research/chi_riverbank, and an unrelated lead (2145, Vázquez Gómez telegrams) for the words 'Mexican codes'. Web search (NYPL Bacon cipher collection Riverbank Mexican codes box 15 Friedman Fabyan intercepts 1917): NYPL catalogue record (30 linear feet, Baconian transcriptions and Riverbank publications) and Friedman lecture notes saying Riverbank worked mainly on Mexican messages; nothing on the contents of boxes 15-16. Missing: an item-level look at the two boxes (NYPL reading room) to see whether they hold message texts at all and whether each has its solution.
